data.title: AI Tops Fed's List of Financial Stability Risks as Concern Surges
data.description:
06:52 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Artificial intelligence was the most frequently cited risk to US financial stability among market participants surveyed by the Federal Reserve, according to the central bank's semiannual Financial Stability Report released Friday.

About 87% of contacts surveyed in September and October named AI as a salient risk, up from 50% in the spring survey. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York polled 23 professionals at broker-dealers, banks, investment funds and advisory firms.

Respondents cited elevated equity valuations, AI-enabled cyberattacks and complex financing tied to data center investment, the Fed said. A correction in risk assets was the second most-cited risk at 52%, followed by higher long-term interest rates at 48%. Cyberattacks and fiscal debt sustainability were each cited by 43%.

Cyberattacks and fiscal debt sustainability were seen as having the most severe potential consequences, the report said. Mentions of AI, higher long-term rates and cyberattacks rose the most from the spring survey, while fewer respondents cited private credit risks, according to the report.

The Fed said advanced computing-related debt issuance topped $680 billion as of October, roughly five times the 2023 total. It said the largest US bank holding companies have close to $1 trillion of exposure to large technology firms, data center developers, related special purpose vehicles, private credit vehicles and utilities.

The Fed said the survey reflects respondents' views and not those of the Fed Board or the New York Fed.

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks mostly ease with tech, Nvidia concerns; airline shares fall late in session
data.description:
(Updates with closing US market levels)

* Nasdaq, S&P 500 end lower

* Oil prices decline for the week

* Dollar extends gains

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Elizabeth Howcroft

NEW YORK/PARIS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Stock indexes mostly fell on Friday as technology shares sold off amid concerns about US chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ), while the dollar was at a 19-month high.

Airline shares dropped in the final minutes of the regular US session after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop of all departing flights. The agency said this was "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety" after it earlier reported serious air traffic control communications issues. The NYSE Arca airline index closed down 1.4%.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended lower, but all three of the major US stock indexes and the pan-European STOXX 600 registered gains for the week.

Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI industry and supply chain given his push to preserve access to the Chinese market and close ties with US President Donald Trump. Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The Philadelphia semiconductor index was down 3.4% and shares of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) were sharply lower. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares finished 2% lower.

"Traders probably weren't excited about carrying positions into the weekend," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana.

"A lot of attention is still going to be paid next week to Nvidia ( NVDA )," he said. The company is due to report quarterly results on Tuesday after the closing bell.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 50.46 points, or 0.10%, to 52,347.55, the S&P 500 fell 30.73 points, or 0.40%, to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 229.82 points, or 0.91%, to 25,136.27. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 both snapped a four-week streak of declines.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 4.15 points, or 0.37%, to 1,112.12.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index ended up just 0.02%, but recorded its best week since late June as strong earnings and a rotation out of tech globally helped investors look past geopolitical risks and the volatility involving AI stocks.

A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was easing on Friday after more than 24 hours of disruption crippled online communications across businesses and governments, though the company said it still had no timeline for full recovery of services.

US 2-YEAR YIELDS HAVE LARGEST WEEKLY RISE IN OVER TWO YEARS

The US dollar index gained for a fourth straight day. Traders this week have been ramping up bets on faster interest rate increases following the consumer price data and hawkish Federal Reserve official commentary.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.17% to 103.40. It hit its highest since April 2025. The euro was down 0.29% at $1.1021.

Investors digested a report showing the US October Producer Price Index for final demand was slightly softer than expected, but still shot up 6.5% year over year. It followed a hotter-than-expected US consumer prices reading earlier this week.

Traders see rising odds that the US central bank could hike rates by a larger-than-usual 50 basis points in December, or raise rates by 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings.

"Inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed's going to need to act a little bit quicker and a little bit more aggressively," said Molly Brooks, US rates strategist at TD Securities.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in an 11% chance of a 50-basis-point hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, which was seen as having zero probability a week ago, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

Treasury yields briefly dipped after the PPI data, but interest-rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields had the largest weekly increase in over two years.

The 2-year note yield was last up 0.34 basis point at 4.867%. It earlier reached 4.892%, the highest since October 14. It registered the biggest weekly increase since the first week of October 2024.

Oil prices were little changed on Friday, but declined for a second straight week. Washington's focus on blockading Iran and ramping up other economic pressures allayed fears of renewed direct conflict in the Iran war.

Brent futures settled at $95.84 a barrel, up 2 cents, or 0.02%. US West Texas Intermediate futures finished at $88.56 a barrel, down 18 cents, or 0.20%. Both Brent and US crude declined for the week.

data.title: Nvidia approaches Arm CEO Haas as employees seek Huang's return, reports say
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times said on Friday, even as another report said some employees were pushing to bring back the former CEO.

Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

Haas' name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang's exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.

He is among several candidates being considered and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, the FT reported. Nvidia's finance chief Colette Kress is currently interim CEO.

Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role and had not formally engaged any potential candidates.

   "Any speculation regarding individual candidates, whether internal or external, is premature," the board said in a statement.

Prior to Huang's resignation, a longtime Nvidia engineer had urged the board in an internal post to consider employee sentiment before taking any action, Wired reported late on Thursday.

The post has since drawn more than 1,600 comments, with several urging the board to find a way to bring Huang back, the technology news platform said, citing internal correspondence it reviewed. Nvidia has about 42,000 employees worldwide.

Billionaire Elon Musk separately said on X that a petition was underway to reinstate Huang and that he would sign it. It was not immediately clear whether Musk was referring to the internal effort reported by Wired.

Nvidia declined to comment on the Wired report as well as Musk's post, while Arm also declined to comment. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

Haas became Arm CEO in 2022, overseeing the company's Nasdaq listing in 2023. Arm designs processor architectures and licenses them to other companies that develop chip designs. Historically its strength has been in mobile phones and it is expanding into computers.

Haas' combination of familiarity with Nvidia and experience running a publicly traded chip company could make him an unusual fit for the role, said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities.

"Rene is one of few external candidates who wouldn't need to be brought up to speed on Nvidia," Boloor said, adding that Haas' understanding of the company's culture alongside his experience running Arm was "a combination you don't find very often."

Arm's US-listed shares closed down about 5%. Nvidia's shares ended the session about 2% lower, bringing market value losses for the week to about $573 billion.

Some analysts expect the next CEO to break from Huang's three-decade reign as the hands-on "chief conductor" who personally steered engineering roadmaps, geopolitical negotiations over exports to China and massive investments across the AI ecosystem.

A potential shift toward a more institutional leadership structure would come as Nvidia faces heightened regulatory scrutiny and a growing consensus among US lawmakers to further restrict the company's chip exports to China.

INSIDERS AND TECH TITANS IN THE RUNNING

Analysts view Kress as a steady financial authority, while veteran engineer Ian Buck is seen as a top candidate after leading development of CUDA, the software platform that powers Nvidia's AI chips.

Apart from Haas, external names discussed by analysts include AMD chief Lisa Su, who has navigated the key China market, and Micron chief Sanjay Mehrotra, whose memory chips power Nvidia servers.

Other candidates cited by industry watchers include Marvell head Matt Murphy and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who oversaw the iPhone maker's in-house silicon development.

Former Apple chief Tim Cook was floated by US President Donald Trump, as Nvidia's board evaluates whether to prioritize financial continuity, deep technical expertise, or experience running a global tech heavyweight.

(Reporting by Kanjyik Ghosh in Barcelona and Anhata Rooprai and Prathik Jayaprakash in Bengaluru; Editing by Arun Koyyur, Sriraj Kalluvila and Leroy Leo)

data.title: Exclusive-Investors flock to Anthropic IPO but question durability of AI lead
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Institutional-investor interest in Anthropic's initial public offering is outpacing the early days of SpaceX's roadshow, according to two people familiar with the companies' offerings.

The Anthropic roadshow is scheduled to run through next Wednesday, when the AI company is expected to price the $64 billion deal. Anthropic and its investment banks are meeting prospective investors in New York, Boston and San Francisco to gauge demand for the offering, one of the people and a third person familiar with the matter said. 

The IPO drew about two times the orders for the shares available by the end of Tuesday, the first day of the roadshow, one of the people said. By the end of Thursday, the book was six times oversubscribed, one other person said. SpaceX's IPO was two times oversubscribed by the end of its second day of roadshow, Reuters previously reported.

While that single-digit subscription rate would be considered modest for many highly anticipated IPOs, bankers and investors said demand is impressive for the Anthropic offering given the size of the IPO. They expect Anthropic's order book to grow substantially as the roadshow progresses, reflecting strong early demand, two of the people said.

Details of the IPO, including the demand for shares, could change, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity. Anthropic declined to comment.

During the roadshow, investors are grappling with two fundamental questions as they assess the offering and the company's valuation: whether Anthropic can maintain its lead as competitors such as Alphabet's Google rapidly catch up in developing advanced AI models, and whether its Claude chatbot can maintain its lead beyond coding, in the broader market for knowledge workers.

TIME OF UNCERTAINTY IN AI

The questions underscore the challenge of valuing a company whose revenue is growing fast but whose long-term competitive position remains uncertain. Investors are trying to determine whether the AI industry will ultimately be dominated by one or two players or support several leading companies, and whether Anthropic can sustain premium pricing if rivals offer comparable models.

Meanwhile, investors are also weighing the limitations of the information Anthropic is providing during its IPO roadshow. One investor who attended a roadshow meeting said the company had not provided detailed answers to some of the questions raised. Anthropic declined to comment on the investor's remarks.

While companies are not always able to address every investor question during roadshows, some investors remain cautious about an offering at a high valuation amid a broader shakeout in the AI sector, with the limited disclosure leaving some questions unanswered.

One of the group meetings during the roadshow also did not include a conference call allowing institutional investors to dial in and ask questions, according to an investor who attended that meeting - a departure from standard roadshow practice. Representatives from Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley largely read from prepared remarks rather than solicit  questions at that meeting, the person added.

Morgan Stanley declined to comment. Goldman Sachs did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

REVENUE AT CENTER OF VALUATION DEBATE

Investors are arriving at widely different estimates of how quickly Anthropic's revenue will grow, creating a broad range of potential valuation outcomes.

The key figure underpinning valuation models is Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue, which banks estimate at around $270 billion to $280 billion and use to apply enterprise-value-to-revenue multiples and arrive at their valuation estimates, two of the people familiar with the projections said. For a high-growth company like Anthropic, investors typically give significant weight to future revenue growth when assessing its value.

Some sell-side projections put Anthropic's revenue at around $52 billion to $53 billion in 2026, rising to $135 billion to $137 billion in  2027, one of the people said.

Certain buy-side projections are running 10% to 15% higher for 2026 and 2027, an investor who has placed an order in the IPO said.

But buy-side forecasts also vary significantly. One investor who conducted due diligence on the IPO but decided not to participate has a more conservative outlook that is about 30% below the sell-side estimate for 2028.

Differences between sell-side and buy-side forecasts are common. Sell-side analysts' estimates tend to track a company's own projections more closely, while investors may build in more optimistic or conservative assumptions about future growth. Companies, in turn, have an incentive to set conservative targets ahead of an IPO, leaving room to beat estimates and raise expectations after listing.

The comparable companies used in the valuation models also reflect the difficulty of finding direct peers for Anthropic. SpaceX and cybersecurity company CrowdStrike are among the names being used as benchmarks, one of the people familiar with the projections said.

The focus on Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue contrasts with SpaceX, whose valuation case relied on projected 2029 revenue that some investors viewed as particularly aggressive. Anthropic's valuation debate, by comparison, is anchored in a forecast for a year closer to its expected public listing. 

​

(Reporting by Milana Vinn and Echo Wang in New York and Krystal Hu in San Francisco, Editing by Colin Barr and Matthew Lewis)

The focus on Anthropic's projected 2028 revenue contrasts with SpaceX, whose valuation case relied on projected 2029 revenue that some investors viewed as particularly aggressive. Anthropic's valuation debate, by comparison, is anchored in a forecast for a year closer to its expected public listing. 

​

(Reporting by Milana Vinn and Echo Wang in New York and Krystal Hu in San Francisco, Editing by Colin Barr and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: White House denies Hassett departing Trump administration
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The White House denied on Friday that National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett was leaving the Trump administration in the coming weeks.

Earlier on Friday, Semafor, citing three people familiar with the plan, reported that Hassett was departing in the coming weeks and had been inquiring about roles outside the administration since before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats retaking both chambers of the US Congress, delivering a blow for Republican President Donald Trump.

"There is no factual basis for this reporting. Kevin Hassett is a key member of President Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance President Trump's economic policies," a White House official said.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who could hold both roles, and his counselor, David Zervos, are among the people being eyed to replace Hassett, according to Semafor. The report said Hassett's plans could change.

Semafor said Hassett's departure would be the latest in a series of staffing changes at the White House. Last week, Trump replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with longtime aide Stephen Miller.

The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Hassett served as the chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers during Trump's first administration.

He left the role in 2019 but later returned to the White House to serve as a senior adviser to Trump during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Hassett was considered to replace Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell last year, but Kevin Warsh eventually got the role.

(Reporting by Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Caitlin Webber)

data.title: FOREX-Dollar set for best week in two months, yen weakens toward 160
data.description:
* Dollar holds firm as traders ramp up rate hike bets

* Fed officials caution on inflation

* Yen just shy of 160 per dollar, stirring intervention worries

* Aussie dollar feels the heat from rising US yields

(Updates headline and prices throughout)

By Chibuike Oguh and Javi West Larrañaga

NEW YORK/GDANSK, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The dollar was on track for its strongest weekly rise in two months on Friday, holding near a 19-month high as rising bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate hike lifted US Treasury yields, while the yen hovered around 160 per dollar and kept traders alert for possible intervention from Tokyo.

Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials and this week's stronger-than-expected US inflation data have left traders weighing the prospect of a larger-than-usual Fed rate hike next month.

Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 34 basis points so far this week to around 4.87%, on course for their biggest weekly jump since April 2025.

The euro was down 0.26% at $1.103, after hitting its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was on course for its fourth straight week of losses.

The dollar was up 0.47% at 0.839 against the Swiss franc and was set to snap two straight weeks of losses.

"The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller."

Traders are pricing in a roughly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was up 0.15% at 103.37, clinging to its highest since April 2025 and on track for its biggest weekly gain since September. That would be its third straight week of gains.

YEN FOCUS

The yen was steady at 159.70 per dollar, around its weakest since early September, fuelling concerns about possible intervention. The currency has weakened about 1% this week, on track for its biggest weekly loss since September.

Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility.

The Australian dollar was down 0.52% at $0.6773. The Aussie is the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is the only G10 country for which markets are pricing a rate cut next year.

The New Zealand kiwi weakened 0.41% versus the greenback to $0.5525 and was on course for its third straight week of losses.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.22% to $68,467.26. Ethereum declined 4.02% to $1,934.86.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York and Javi West Larrañaga in Gdansk; Editing by Susan Fenton and Edmund Klamann)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Nvidia approaches Arm CEO Haas as employees seek Huang's return, media reports say
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, even as Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees pushed for their former CEO's return, according to a separate media report.

An internal Nvidia ( NVDA ) post urging the board to consider employee sentiment over Huang's future has drawn more than 1,600 comments, with several calling for his reinstatement, technology news platform Wired reported on Thursday, citing internal correspondence it reviewed.

Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

Haas' name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang's exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia ( NVDA ), rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.

He is among several candidates being considered and there is no guarantee he will be offered the job or accept it, the FT reported. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) finance chief Colette Kress is currently interim CEO.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role and had not formally engaged any potential candidates.

   "Any speculation regarding individual candidates, whether internal or external, is premature," the board said in a statement.

Billionaire Elon Musk separately said on X that a petition was underway to reinstate Huang and that he would sign it. It was not immediately clear whether Musk was referring to the internal effort reported by Wired.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the Wired report or Musk's X post, while Arm Holdings declined to comment. Reuters could not independently verify the reports.

Haas became Arm CEO in 2022, overseeing the company's Nasdaq listing in 2023. Arm designs processor architectures and licenses them to other companies that develop chip designs. Historically its strength has been in mobile phones and it is expanding into computers.

Haas' combination of familiarity with Nvidia ( NVDA ) and experience running a publicly traded chip company could make him an unusual fit for the role, said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities.

"Rene is one of few external candidates who wouldn't need to be brought up to speed on Nvidia ( NVDA )," Boloor said, adding that Haas' understanding of the company's culture alongside his experience running Arm was "a combination you don't find very often."

Arm's US-listed shares closed down about 5%. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares closed about 2% lower, bringing their market value losses for the week to about $573 billion.

Some analysts expect the next CEO to break from Huang's three-decade reign as the hands-on "chief conductor" who personally steered engineering roadmaps, geopolitical negotiations over China exports and massive investments across the AI ecosystem.

A potential shift toward a more institutional leadership structure would come as Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces heightened regulatory scrutiny and a growing consensus among US lawmakers to further restrict the company's chip exports to China.

INSIDERS AND TECH TITANS IN THE RUNNING

Analysts view Kress as a steady financial authority, while veteran engineer Ian Buck is seen as a top candidate after leading development of CUDA, the software platform that powers Nvidia's ( NVDA ) AI chips.

Apart from Haas, external names discussed by analysts include AMD chief Lisa Su, who has navigated the key China market, and Micron chief Sanjay Mehrotra, whose memory chips power Nvidia ( NVDA ) servers.

Other candidates cited by industry watchers include Marvell head Matt Murphy and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who oversaw the iPhone maker's in-house silicon development.

Former Apple chief Tim Cook was floated by US President Donald Trump, as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board evaluates whether to prioritize financial continuity, deep technical expertise, or experience running a global tech heavyweight.

(Reporting by Kanjyik Ghosh in Barcelona and Anhata Rooprai and Prathik Jayaprakash in Bengaluru; Editing by Arun Koyyur, Sriraj Kalluvila and Leroy Leo)

data.title: XMax Inc. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XMax Inc. ( XMAX ) , a distributor of contemporary furniture and artificial intelligence software and platform-based service provider, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Revenue: $6.4 million, down 34% from $9.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, including $4.5 million from API-based services and $1.9 million from furniture (down 81%, as the prior-year period included a $7.9 million marble slab liquidation sale)
  • Gross Profit: $0.9 million, representing a 14% gross margin, compared to gross profit of $1.0 million and gross margin of 10% for the third quarter of 2025
  • Net Loss: $(9.0) million, driven primarily by a $10.5 million non-cash unrealized loss on the Company's investment in Preamble Capital and partially offset by a $3.6 million deferred tax benefit, compared to a net loss of $(1.1) million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Cash and Cash Equivalents: $10.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $6.7 million at December 31, 2025
  • Working Capital: $22.0 million as of September 30, 2026, up from $9.4 million at December 31, 2025

Management Commentary

“The third quarter of 2026 was a period of rapid scaling for XMax ( XMAX ) as our API-based services generated $4.5 million of revenue, their first full quarter of contribution,” said Xiaohua Lu, Chief Executive Officer of the Company. “We reported a net loss of $9.0 million for the quarter, driven primarily by a $10.5 million non-cash unrealized loss on our investment in Preamble Capital, partly offset by a $3.6 million deferred tax benefit. For the first nine months, net income was $23.6 million, while our balance sheet was supported by approximately $10.6 million in cash, $22.0 million in working capital and a $79.3 million investment in Preamble Capital funds as of September 30, 2026.”

“Our overall gross margin was 14% in the third quarter, compared to 10% a year ago, when results included a low-margin marble slab liquidation sale. Furniture gross margin was 51%, while our API-based services were approximately break-even at the gross level as we scale,” Mr. Lu continued. “Total revenue declined 34% to $6.4 million as furniture sales fell 81% to $1.9 million, reflecting the prior-year liquidation sale, challenging market conditions and tariffs, only partly offset by $4.5 million from our API-based services. With working capital of $22.0 million, up from $9.4 million at year-end, we have financial flexibility to pursue our strategic AI initiatives.”

“Looking ahead, our priority is to scale our AI offerings through XMax AI Inc. in the U.S. and Elonx AI Holdings PTE. LTD. in Singapore, while allocating capital with discipline to build long-term value for our shareholders,” Mr. Lu added. “In October, we signed an agreement for dedicated NVIDIA B300 GPU capacity of up to 512 GPUs, subject to closing conditions. Combined with our live API platform, this would meaningfully expand the compute we can offer enterprise customers building AI into their products and operations.”

“We are also committed to returning value to shareholders,” Mr. Lu added. “In October, our Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $30 million, to be funded from existing cash and shares shall be repurchased at prices below $5.50 per share and the Company has commenced repurchases of its common stock on November 5, 2026 through its engaged broker-dealer with purchases made from time to time in the open market in accordance with Rule 10b-18.”

Headquartered in Commerce, California, XMax Inc. ( XMAX ) , formerly known as Nova LifeStyle, Inc., is a diversified company engaged in the design, sourcing, and distribution of contemporary furniture, as well as the development of artificial intelligence technologies and applications. The Company operates through an established global network of suppliers, distributors, and e-commerce channels, serving a broad customer base. In addition, the Company is expanding into artificial intelligence technologies, including AI software and platform-based services through its wholly owned subsidiaries XMax AI Inc. and Elonx AI Holdings PTE. LTD., to support future growth. By leveraging emerging technologies, the Company aims to drive diversification and long-term value creation.

data.title: Epic Games adds to legal lineup for Supreme Court showdown with Apple
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - 'Fortnite' maker Epic Games has added a seasoned US Supreme Court lawyer from Mayer Brown to its legal team as it prepares for a high-stakes clash with Apple ( AAPL ) in January over a ruling that found the iPhone maker in contempt of court.

Here are some details:

* Epic's legal team now includes Mayer Brown's Nicole Saharsky, who appeared on the company's filing on Friday urging the justices to reject Apple's ( AAPL ) appeal. Saharsky, who has argued 32 cases at the Supreme Court, is working with Epic's longtime legal team at Cravath, Swaine & Moore

* The justices on January 11 will hear Apple's ( AAPL ) appeal of a ruling holding the company in contempt of a court's injunction that mandated sweeping changes to its lucrative App Store

* "Rather than complying with the district court's order, Apple ( AAPL ) started charging a 27% junk fee on purchases made on the open web, and then made it nearly impossible for customers to link out to make those purchases," Epic said in a statement on social media. "Contempt is for companies that knowingly violate court orders."

* Epic won the injunction in a lawsuit it filed in 2020 contesting Apple's ( AAPL ) app store fees. The lawsuit challenged Apple's ( AAPL ) control over transactions in applications that use the company's iOS operating system and its ​restrictions on how apps are distributed to consumers

* Apple ( AAPL ) denies it has violated the order, saying that the text of the injunction did not mention commissions. The company, represented by former US solicitor general Gregory Garre of Latham & Watkins, said it can't be held in contempt for "an after-the-fact assessment of an order's unstated 'spirit'."

The case is Apple Inc ( AAPL ) v. Epic Games Inc, US Supreme Court, No. 25-1311.

For Apple ( AAPL ): Gregory Garre of Latham & Watkins

For Epic: Nicole Saharsky of Mayer Brown

(Reporting by Mike Scarcella)

data.title: Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund Announces Results for the Third Quarter of 2026 and Tightens 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance to Between $495 and $515 Million
data.description:
Announces appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (“PwC”) as the Fund’s new external auditor for fiscal 2027

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund ( CGIFF ) (“Chemtrade” or the “Fund”) today announced results for the three and nine-month period ended September 30, 2026. The financial statements and MD&A will be available on Chemtrade’s website at www.chemtradelogistics.com and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.com.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue of $633.1 million, an increase of $100.4 million or 18.8% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, revenue for 2026 was $92.9 million higher than 2025, driven by higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products and Regen acid in the ASP segment as well as revenue related to the Polytec acquisition in the WS segment. This more than offset lower selling prices for chlor-alkali products and lower volumes of sodium chlorate in the EC segment.
  • Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $145.1 million, a decrease of $6.1 million or 4.0% year-over-year; excluding the impact of foreign exchange, Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million lower than 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from the Polytec acquisition, lower corporate costs and higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products were not sufficient to offset lower selling prices for chlor-alkali products and lower volumes of sodium chlorate. Adjusted EBITDA for water products was also lower as higher selling prices did not fully offset higher input costs.
  • Net earnings of $47.3 million, an increase of $5.0 million year-over-year primarily due to lower finance costs partially offset by lower Adjusted EBITDA, higher income tax expense and higher depreciation and amortization expense.
  • Cash flows from operating activities of $156.1 million, an increase of $5.9 million or 3.9% year-over-year, mainly due to decreases in working capital and interest paid compared to 2025, partially offset by lower Adjusted EBITDA.
  • Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures(1) of $75.7 million, a decrease of $2.1 million or 2.7% year-over-year reflecting lower Adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by lower maintenance capital expenditures(1). Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures per unit(1) of $0.68 was $0.01 lower year-over-year.
  • During the first quarter of 2026, Chemtrade increased its monthly distribution by approximately 4% to $0.06 per unit or $0.72 per unit per year. Chemtrade’s Payout ratio(1) for the third quarter of 2026 was 27% and for the last twelve months was 46%.
  • During the third quarter of 2026, Chemtrade purchased approximately 1.0 million units as part of its normal course issuer bid (NCIB). Under its current NCIB, which terminates on April 16, 2027, Chemtrade is authorized to purchase approximately 5.8 million units of which approximately 3.6 million remain available for purchase as of November 10, 2026.
  • Chemtrade continues to maintain a prudent balance sheet, with a Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA(1) ratio of 2.48x at the end of the third quarter of 2026.
  • Due to geopolitical events, several of Chemtrade’s key products and raw material inputs have seen significant price volatility during 2026. Despite this volatility, Chemtrade’s 2026 Adjusted EBITDA expectations continue to be largely in line with the guidance issued at the beginning of the year but now within a tighter range of $495.0 to $515.0 million.
  • After a comprehensive request for proposal process for external audit services, the Fund’s Board of Trustees has approved the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the Fund’s external auditor for fiscal 2027. KPMG LLP will continue to serve as the Fund’s external auditor through the financial year ending December 31, 2026.

(1) Adjusted EBITDA is a Total of Segments measure, Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures is a non-IFRS measure and Net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA, Distributable cash after maintenance and capital expenditures per unit and Payout ratio are non-IFRS ratios. Maintenance capital expenditures is a Supplementary financial measure. Please see Non-IFRS and Other Financial Measures for more information.

Scott Rook, President and CEO of Chemtrade, commented, “Our third quarter results reflected a continuation of the trends of the second quarter as the stability of the ASP and WS segments was offset by the softness of EC, particularly in chlor-alkali. However, our diversified product mix, operational excellence, and exceptional team continue to demonstrate resilience and to deliver strong results.”

Sulphur costs remained at historically high levels in the third quarter. Our ASP segment is largely insulated from sulphur price changes, but higher costs have been a headwind in WS despite our team being able to offset more than 80% of cost increases through pricing adjustments this year. There are signs that sulphur costs are starting to ease as demonstrated by fourth quarter sulphur settling 13% below the third quarter, which is expected to support WS margins. With 2026 nearly complete, we expect a substantial improvement in the fourth quarter over the same period in 2025. I would like to thank our entire team for the dedication and agility that position Chemtrade to deliver near-record annual results despite challenging market conditions,” continued Mr. Rook.

“We remain committed to the growth targets in our Vision 2030 strategic framework, supported by our strong balance sheet. We ended the quarter at our target leverage, and for the right inorganic growth opportunity we are prepared to let it rise modestly into the higher 2x range.”

“Over the past few years, Chemtrade has transformed through reliability, productivity improvements, pricing discipline and organic growth investments. We intend to continue the transformation by converting from an income trust to a corporation, which we believe will, among other benefits, broaden our investor base. Subject to Board approval, we expect to continue our balanced approach to capital allocation: eligible dividends, share repurchases under our active NCIB, and growth investments. We urge our unitholders to vote in favour of the conversion,” concluded Mr. Rook.

Consolidated Financial Summary of Q3 2026

The Canadian dollar weakened by $0.02 relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the third quarter of 2025, contributing positively to consolidated revenue and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA by $7.5 million and $2.2 million, respectively.

Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $633.1 million, an increase of $100.4 or 18.8% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, revenue was $92.9 million higher than the prior year period. The increase was due to (i) higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products, and Regen acid in the ASP segment; and (ii) revenue from the acquisition of Polytec as well as higher selling prices for water solutions products in the WS segment. These gains were partially offset by (i) lower volumes of sodium chlorate in the EC segment; and (ii) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products partially offset by higher volumes in the EC segment.

Adjusted EBITDA was $145.1 million, a decrease of $6.1 million or 4.0% year-over-year. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, Adjusted EBITDA was $8.3 million lower than the prior year period. The decrease was primarily due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products as well as lower sales volumes for sodium chlorate in the EC segment; and (ii) lower margins for water solutions products in the WS segment. A partial offset was provided by (i) lower corporate costs; (ii) Adjusted EBITDA contribution from the Polytec acquisition in the WS segment; and (iii) higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products in the ASP segment.

Distributable cash after maintenance capital expenditures for the third quarter of 2026 was $75.7 million or $0.68 per unit, compared with $77.8 million or $0.69 per unit in the third quarter of 2025. The year-over year change primarily reflects lower Adjusted EBITDA, partially offset by lower maintenance capital expenditures and a lower number of units. Chemtrade’s payout ratio for the twelve months ended September 30, 2026 was 46%.

The timing of maintenance capex in 2026 is significantly different than 2025. During 2025, approximately one-third of the annual maintenance capex was incurred during the fourth quarter, whereas less than one-third is expected to be incurred in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Chemtrade maintained a strong balance sheet through the third quarter of 2026. As of September 30, 2026, Chemtrade’s Net debt was $1.2 billion and its Net Debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA ratio was 2.48x. As of the end of the third quarter of 2026, Chemtrade also maintained ample financial liquidity with approximately $461 million (US$324 million) undrawn on its credit facilities, in addition to $55.7 million of cash on hand.

Segmented Financial Summary of Q3 2026

As of 2026, Chemtrade has separated the former Sulphur and Water Chemicals (SWC) segment into two new segments, the Acid and Sulphur Products (ASP) segment and the Water Solutions (WS) segment. Chemtrade now reports its results in three segments:

  • The ASP segment markets, removes, and/or produces merchant, Regen, and ultrapure acid, sodium nitrite, all other sulphur-related products, and provides other processing services.
  • The WS, segment manufactures and markets a variety of inorganic coagulants used in water treatment, including aluminum sulphate (alum), aluminum chlorohydrate (ACH), polyaluminum chloride (PACl), and ferric sulphate (ferric). WS also provides value-added water solutions.
  • The Electrochemicals (EC), segment manufactures and markets sodium chlorate and chlor-alkali products including caustic soda, chlorine and hydrochloric acid, largely for the pulp and paper, oil and gas, and water treatment industries. These products are marketed primarily to North American and South American customers.

The ASP segment reported revenue of $231.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $176.9 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the ASP segment was $52.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $51.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the third quarter of 2025 had a positive impact on ASP revenue and ASP Adjusted EBITDA of $3.2 million and $0.7 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, ASP revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $51.0 million or 28.8% year-over-year. The increase in comparable ASP revenue was primarily due to higher selling prices for merchant acid, sulphur products, and Regen acid. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, ASP Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $0.9 million or 1.8% year-over-year. The increase in comparable ASP Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to higher Adjusted EBITDA for sulphur products.

The WS segment reported revenue of $210.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $157.2 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the WS segment was $40.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $41.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 had a positive year-over-year impact on WS revenue and WS Adjusted EBITDA of $2.5 million and $0.2 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, WS revenue in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $50.7 million or 32.3% year-over-year. The increase in WS revenue was primarily due to additional revenue from the Polytec acquisition and higher selling prices for water solutions products. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, WS Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $1.2 million or 2.9% year-over-year. The decrease in comparable WS Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to lower margins for water solutions products partially offset by additional Adjusted EBITDA from the Polytec acquisition. Higher selling prices for water solutions products offset approximately 80% of the higher input costs.

The EC segment reported revenue of $191.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $198.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA in the EC segment was $74.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $93.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. The weaker Canadian dollar relative to the U.S. dollar during the third quarter of 2026 had a positive year-over-year impact on EC revenue and EC Adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 million and $1.4 million, respectively.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, EC revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $8.8 million or 4.4% lower compared to the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in EC revenue was primarily due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products, partially offset by higher volumes; and (ii) lower volumes for sodium chlorate. MECU netbacks decreased by approximately $260 year-over-year with approximately 95% of the decline attributable to hydrochloric acid and chlorine. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange, as noted above, EC Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was $20.5 million or 21.9% lower year-over-year due to (i) lower MECU netbacks for chlor-alkali products; and (ii) lower volumes for sodium chlorate.

Corporate costs for the third quarter of 2026 were $22.4 million, compared with $34.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in corporate costs was primarily due to (i) $9.5 million of lower long-term incentive compensation costs; (ii) $2.5 million of lower short-term incentive compensation costs; and (iii) $2.0 million of legal and other costs in 2025 related to the Polytec acquisition. Higher realized foreign exchange losses of $0.8 million were a partial offset.

2026 Guidance

Due to geopolitical events, several of Chemtrade’s key products and raw material inputs have seen significant price volatility during 2026. Despite this volatility, Chemtrade’s 2026 Adjusted EBITDA expectations continue to be largely in line with the guidance issued at the beginning of the year but now within a tighter range of $495.0 to $515.0 million. Based on current guidance assumptions, including the anticipated spending on Growth capital expenditures and changes in capital allocation, Chemtrade expects to end 2026 with a Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio of close to 2.5x and an implied Payout ratio of approximately 40%.

At the midpoint of this guidance range, Chemtrade’s Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 would be comparable to the historically high level achieved in 2025, highlighting the significant step-change in Chemtrade’s Adjusted EBITDA and cashflow generation in the last five years

The timing of maintenance capex in 2026 is significantly different than 2025. During 2025, approximately one-third of the annual maintenance capex was incurred during the fourth quarter, whereas less than one-third is expected to be incurred in the fourth quarter of 2026.

As of November 10th, 2026, approximately 3.6 million units remain available for purchase. Purchases of units are effected through the facilities of the TSX and/or alternative Canadian trading systems and are made by means of open market transactions, or such other means as may be permitted by the TSX, including block purchases of units, at prevailing market rates. The timing and amount of any purchases are subject to management’s discretion.

Chemtrade’s management and Board of Trustees continue to assess opportunities to further adjust and optimize its capital structure. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, Chemtrade took steps to optimize its balance sheet and liquidity as outlined in this press release and third quarter financial disclosures.

Rohit Bhardwaj, CFO of Chemtrade, commented on Chemtrade’s financial position and capital allocation, “Despite the uncertain and volatile macroeconomic backdrop, Chemtrade maintains a prudent balance sheet and continues to act on opportunities that improve its financial position. To that effect, subsequent to the end of the third quarter, we issued $200 million of 5.75% senior unsecured notes that mature in 2032 while extending and upsizing our credit facility.

We exited Q3 2026 with on-target leverage of 2.5x Net Debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA, which provides the financial flexibility to execute on various growth strategies as they may arise. Although we may allow a slightly above target leverage for a short period of time, the upper bound remains in the high 2x range. Our disciplined capital allocation strategy is designed to provide a healthy balance of debt reduction, sustainable earnings growth, and returning of capital to unitholders via the NCIB and (eligible) dividends should our proposed conversion to a corporation achieve unitholder approval later in 2026,” concluded Mr. Bhardwaj.

Senior unsecured notes maturing October 1, 2032

On October 20, 2026, Chemtrade closed the private placement of $200.0 million aggregate principal notes (“the “Notes”) via the reopening of the 5.75% senior unsecured notes maturing October 1, 2032. The Notes were issued at a price of $982.50 per $1,000 principal amount (yield of 6.104%), plus accrued interest from and including October 1, 2026. The Notes have identical terms (except for their date of issue and issuance price) as, and form part of a single series with, the $250.0 million aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2032 issued by the Company on October 1, 2025, resulting in an aggregate of $450.0 million principal amount outstanding of 5.750% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2032. The net proceeds of the offering were used to reduce indebtedness and for general corporate purposes.

Extension of Credit Facility

Subsequent to September 30, 2026, Chemtrade extended and upsized its credit facility. The updated credit facility has a limit of US$700.0 million (from US$600.0 million prior) and a maturity date of November 9, 2031 (from October 31, 2030 prior).

Trust Conversion

On October 9, 2026, Chemtrade announced a proposed conversion of the Fund from an income trust to a corporate structure pursuant to a court-approved statutory plan of arrangement (the “Plan”), and subject to the terms and conditions set forth in an arrangement agreement entered into between the Fund and Chemtrade Inc. (“PubCo”) dated October 9, 2026 (the “Arrangement Agreement”).

On November 3, 2026, the Fund obtained an interim order (the “Interim Order”) from the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) in respect of the Plan, authorizing, among other things, the calling and holding of a special meeting of Unitholders (the “Special Meeting”) to consider and vote on the Plan.

Complete details of the terms of the Plan and a copy of the Arrangement Agreement will be provided in an information circular (the “Meeting Circular”) to Unitholders entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Special Meeting. The Meeting Circular will be mailed to entitled Unitholders and will be made available and filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca as well as on Chemtrade’s Investor Relations section of its website at www.chemtradelogistics.com/investors, on or about November 16, 2026. Unitholders are strongly urged to review and evaluate the information in the Meeting Circular once received or accessed.

The Plan will be subject to Unitholder approval at the Special Meeting, expected to be held on December 7, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern Standard Time). The Plan must be approved by at least 66 2/3% of the votes cast by Unitholders voting in person or by proxy at the Special Meeting.

Change in Auditors

After a comprehensive request for proposal (“RFP”) process for external audit services, the Fund’s Board of Trustees has approved the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (“PwC”) as the Fund’s external auditor for fiscal 2027. KPMG LLP (“KPMG”) will continue to serve as the Fund’s external auditor through the financial year ending December 31, 2026.

Consistent with Fund’s commitment to strong governance and oversight, the Audit Committee of the Board of Trustees initiated the RFP in recognition of KPMG’s long tenure as the Fund’s external auditor. Following a thorough evaluation, the Board of Trustees, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, selected PwC on the basis of its depth of expertise, qualifications, and independence.

The Fund thanks KPMG for its 26 years of service as the Fund’s auditor and for the valuable insight and professional stewardship it has provided over that time.

At the Fund’s request, KPMG will resign as external auditor effective on the first business day following the filing of the Fund’s audited consolidated financial statements for the year ending December 31, 2026 and KPMG’s auditor’s report thereon. PwC will be appointed on the same day to fill the resulting vacancy and will hold office until the Fund’s 2027 annual meeting of unitholders, at which the Fund intends to propose the appointment of PwC as external auditor for the ensuing year.

There have been no modified opinions in KPMG’s reports on the Fund’s financial statements for the two most recently completed fiscal years, and in the opinion of the Fund there have been no “reportable events” (as defined in National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations) between the Fund and KPMG. The Fund’s Notice of Change of Auditor, together with the letters from KPMG and PwC, will be filed on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Chemtrade operates a diversified business providing industrial chemicals and services to customers in North and South America. Chemtrade is one of North America’s largest suppliers of sulphuric acid, spent acid processing services, inorganic coagulants for water treatment, sodium chlorate, sodium nitrite and sodium hydrosulphite. Chemtrade is also a leading producer of high purity sulphuric acid for the semiconductor industry in North America. Hsinchu, Taiwan, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MKDWELL Tech Inc. ( MKDW ) (the “Company”) , an automotive electronics manufacturer, today announced that its Board of Directors has approved a Reverse Share Split on its ordinary shares and class A preferred shares on a one-for-twenty basis (the “Reverse Share Split”). The Reverse Share Split will take effect at 9:00 a.m., Eastern Time, on November 18, 2026 (the “Effective Time”).

The ordinary shares will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the existing symbol “MKDW” and will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on November 18, 2026. The new CUSIP number for the ordinary share following the Reverse Share Split will be G6209W132.

At the Effective Time, every twenty ordinary shares of the Company will be automatically reclassified and combined into one ordinary share with no par value. As a result of the Reverse Share Split, the number of issued and outstanding ordinary shares will reduce from 36,354,390 shares (the number of ordinary shares issued and outstanding as of November 12, 2026) to approximately 1,817,720 shares. The Company also holds 1,212,667 ordinary shares as treasury shares, which will be reduced to 60,634 shares. 274,367 class A preferred shares each having no par value will be reduced to 13,719 shares. All of such class A preferred shares are held by Mr. Ming-Chia Huang, the Company’s chief executive officer and director. Each ordinary share entitles the holder to one vote per share, and each class A preferred share entitles the holder to 100 votes per share. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Share Split and fractional amounts will be rounded up to the nearest whole number at the participant level.

Additionally, at the Effective Time, proportionate adjustments will be made, based on the one-for-twenty ratio, to the number of ordinary shares issuable upon exercise of the Company’s outstanding warrants to purchase one ordinary share (the “Warrants”), including a proportional decrease in the number of ordinary shares issuable upon exercise of each Warrant and a corresponding proportional increase in the exercise price of each Warrant. This adjustment is additional to the previous adjustment made in January 26, 2026, when the Company completed a one-for-thirty reverse split of its ordinary shares and class A preferred shares.

The Reverse Share Split is a proactive measure as part of the Company’s strategic plan to maintain compliance with Nasdaq’s continued listing requirements, while also strengthening the Company’s long-term capital structure.

About MKDWELL Tech Inc. ( MKDW )

Through its operating subsidiaries, MKDWELL Tech Inc. ( MKDW ) manufactures and supplies automotive electronics for passenger cars, modified commercial vehicles, camper vans and logistics vehicles. Its business covers research and development, design, production and sales, with a focus on intelligent control systems and LiDAR sensors. Through its operating subsidiaries, the Company also conducts smart-home and Internet-of-Things (IoT) product businesses and provides OEM and ODM solutions for international brand and retail customers. The Company’s operations span Taiwan, mainland China and Hong Kong.

By Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index ended lower on Friday as technology shares fell, but the index still notched a weekly gain as recent strength in corporate profits offset worries about higher interest rates to tackle inflation.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended down 31.29 points, or 0.1%, at 36,105.90. For the week, the index gained 0.9%, its second straight weekly advance.

* US stocks posted steeper declines on Friday as concerns about Nvidia ( NVDA ) pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

* "It's a mixed day, ending an up-week. So that theme of resilience continues," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones. "We have corporate profits which continue to exceed expectations ... That is helping to provide a significant offset to a lot of the concerns about AI, technology and inflation."

* Economists expect Canada's consumer price index report for October, due on Monday, to show inflation rising to an annual rate of 3.2%.

* "If there are any takeaways from this week's US inflation data is that there are some lingering pressures, (and) that policymakers are running out of patience," Kourkafas said.

* Investors see a 64% chance the Bank of Canada will raise interest rates in December.

* The TSX's technology sector fell 1.3%, with shares of electronic equipment company Celestica ( CLS ) down 5.4%.

* Heavily weighted financials and the materials group, which includes metal mining shares, posted declines of 0.2% and 0.6% respectively. The price of copper was down 2%.

* Most other sectors notched gains, including energy, which added 0.9%.

* US crude oil futures settled 0.2% lower and posted their second straight weekly decline, as signs of a growing global supply surplus weighed on the market.

* The consumer staples sector rose 0.8%, while industrials ended 0.2% higher, led by Stantec ( STN ) .

data.title: Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) has said US export controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-centre market, but a Reuters review has identified more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around the American chipmaker's restricted processors.

The projects, stretching from China's wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia ( NVDA ) hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing's access to the technology powering the global artificial-intelligence boom.

The Reuters review examined more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures, identifying projects and equipment agreements with a combined reported value exceeding 23 billion yuan ($3.2 billion).

The findings paint a detailed picture of how deeply Nvidia ( NVDA ) technology remains embedded in China's AI expansion. They reveal the company's technology reaches well beyond China's largest tech firms, into local government-backed ventures, universities and regional computing centres.

The estimate includes planned investments and signed contracts as well as completed installations. It covers buildings, power systems and other infrastructure, and does not reflect spending on Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips alone.

China's commerce ministry and Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immedietely respond to Reuters request for comment.

The findings come a day after Nvidia ( NVDA ) co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive amid a scandal over his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of intelligence ties to Beijing.

Huang, a vocal advocate of easing export restrictions, said last year Nvidia's ( NVDA ) market share in China had fallen from 95% to zero. The company has also excluded China data-centre computing revenue from its forecasts, citing regulatory uncertainty.

That does not mean Chinese demand has disappeared. While Nvidia's ( NVDA ) statements address its own ability to compete and sell directly in China, the documents Reuters reviewed show Chinese customers continuing to plan purchases and, in some cases, operating restricted processors.

Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Reuters' findings reinforce his own view on enforcement: "Washington must stop focusing solely on who buys the chips on the surface and start examining who ultimately uses the computing power-and for what purpose." 

BILLIONS IN THE PIPELINE

Across China, developers and institutions are advancing billions of dollars in AI data-centre projects designed around restricted Nvidia H100, H200, and H800 processors. These range from massive regional computing hubs to retrofitted commercial sites - such as a facility in northwestern Gansu province that was expected to install thousands of Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips before year-end, though it remains unclear if those processors ever arrived.

While some facilities are already operational or under construction, operators are exposed to potential delays, supply disruptions, or costly redesigns around domestic chips as export controls tighten. 

Huang's departure could deepen these vulnerabilities by weakening Nvidia's ( NVDA ) lobbying leverage as US lawmakers press for tighter controls.

WASHINGTON'S DILEMMA

Washington began restricting Nvidia's ( NVDA ) advanced AI processors in 2022 and subsequently tightened controls on modified chips developed for China, including the H800.

In January, the Trump administration moved to review H200 export licences for eligible Chinese customers individually, subject to conditions.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) August filing said it was effectively excluded from China's data-centre computing market. But an IDC report cited by Reuters in October estimated Nvidia ( NVDA ) still accounted for 34% of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in the first half of 2026.

The figures measure different things and do not establish how the restricted hardware identified in the Reuters investigation reached Chinese users.

The scrutiny has intensified since Huang's resignation on Thursday, following allegations involving Alice Huang, a former executive associated with Singapore-based Nvidia ( NVDA ) cloud partner Megaspeed.

Megaspeed has denied illegally diverting Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips to China. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board launched an independent investigation, saying it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security were compromised. There has been no public finding that Jensen Huang violated export-control laws.

The Chinese projects identified by Reuters have not been linked to Megaspeed or the allegations involving Huang.

(Reporting by Eduardo BaptistaEditing by Shri Navaratnam)
